newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Marxist rebels free seven more hostages.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Marxist rebels free seven more hostages.

text.p: Peruvian Marxist guerrillas freed on Wednesday seven more hostages, leaving 74 inside the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
The captives, all wearing jackets and looking in good health, walked out of the building with chief Red Cross representative Michel Minnig and Peruvian Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani.
It was not immediately clear who all the newly freed men were, although one was identified as Peruvian privatization official Juan Assereto Duaret.

Cipriani, a close ally of Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori, has been acting as an observer in the hostage crisis. "Please let's continue praying to the Virgin Mary, queen of the peace, so that she helps us continue the path of peace," he told reporters outside the residence.
The seven men were taken in a waiting bus to a police hospital for a routine medical checkup.
